stem: The distance moved by an object in a unit of time is called its __________.
solution: Speed is the distance travelled per unit time.

stem: The SI unit of speed is __________.
solution: The SI unit of speed is metre per second (m/s).

stem: Speed is calculated using the formula __________.
solution: Speed = total distance travelled ÷ total time taken.

stem: A car travels 100 km in 2 hours. Its speed is __________.
solution: Speed = 100 km ÷ 2 h = 50 km/h.

stem: An object that covers equal distances in equal intervals of time is said to be in __________.
solution: In uniform motion, an object covers equal distances in equal time intervals, i.e., constant speed.

stem: An object that covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time is in __________.
solution: Non-uniform motion means the object's speed changes, covering unequal distances in equal times.

stem: The SI unit of time is the __________.
solution: The SI unit of time is the second (s).

stem: One of the earliest natural events used to measure time was the __________.
options: periodic motions like day and night and phases of the Moon
solution: Ancient people measured time using periodic natural events like day/night and lunar phases.

stem: The device that measures time using the regular swings of a pendulum is a __________.
solution: A pendulum clock uses the regular oscillations of a pendulum to keep time.

stem: The to-and-fro motion of a pendulum is an example of __________ motion.
solution: A pendulum repeats its swing at regular intervals — periodic (oscillatory) motion.

stem: The time taken by a pendulum to complete one full oscillation is called its __________.
solution: The time period is the time for one complete oscillation of the pendulum.

stem: The time period of a simple pendulum depends mainly on its __________.
solution: The time period of a simple pendulum depends on its length (longer pendulums swing more slowly).

stem: 1 hour is equal to __________ seconds.
solution: 1 hour = 60 minutes × 60 seconds = 3600 seconds.

stem: The speed of a vehicle is often shown by an instrument called the __________.
solution: A speedometer indicates the instantaneous speed of a vehicle.

stem: The instrument that records the total distance travelled by a vehicle is the __________.
solution: The odometer records the total distance covered by a vehicle.

stem: On a distance–time graph, the motion of an object at rest is shown by a __________.
solution: When an object is at rest, distance does not change with time, giving a horizontal line.

stem: On a distance–time graph, uniform motion is represented by a __________.
solution: Uniform motion (constant speed) gives a straight, sloping line on a distance–time graph.

stem: On a distance–time graph, a steeper slope indicates __________.
solution: A steeper line means more distance is covered per unit time, i.e., a greater speed.

stem: A simple pendulum consists of a small metal ball (bob) suspended by a __________.
solution: A simple pendulum is a small bob hung by a light, inextensible thread from a fixed point.

stem: A train covers 240 km in 4 hours. Its average speed is __________.
solution: Speed = 240 km ÷ 4 h = 60 km/h.

stem: To convert a speed from km/h to m/s, we multiply by __________.
solution: 1 km/h = 1000 m / 3600 s = 5/18 m/s, so multiply km/h by 5/18 to get m/s.

stem: The average speed of an object is found by dividing the __________.
options: total distance by the total time
solution: Average speed = total distance travelled ÷ total time taken.

stem: Sundials measure time by using the __________.
options: position of the shadow cast by the Sun
solution: A sundial uses the moving shadow of the Sun to indicate the time of day.

stem: Which of the following is used to measure very small intervals of time, such as in races?
solution: A stopwatch measures short time intervals precisely, useful in sports.

stem: Modern clocks and watches often keep accurate time using the vibrations of a __________ crystal.
solution: Quartz clocks use the regular vibrations of a quartz crystal to keep accurate time.

stem: A body moving in a straight line with changing speed is in __________.
solution: Changing speed along a straight line is non-uniform (straight-line) motion.

stem: If a bus covers 30 km in the first hour and 50 km in the second hour, its motion is __________.
solution: Different distances in equal time intervals mean the motion is non-uniform.

stem: The speed of a moving object tells us __________.
options: how fast or slow it is moving
solution: Speed indicates how fast an object is moving.

stem: The larger unit of speed used for vehicles on roads is usually __________.
solution: Vehicle speeds are conveniently expressed in kilometres per hour (km/h).

stem: On a distance–time graph, time is usually taken along the __________.
solution: By convention, time is plotted on the horizontal x-axis and distance on the vertical y-axis.

stem: A pendulum with a longer thread will have a __________ time period than a shorter one.
solution: A longer pendulum swings more slowly, so its time period is greater.

stem: If the time period of a pendulum is 2 seconds, then in 1 minute it makes __________ oscillations.
solution: 60 s ÷ 2 s per oscillation = 30 oscillations in a minute.

stem: Which of the following is an example of periodic motion used to measure time?
options: A car braking to a stop
solution: A pendulum's regular oscillation is periodic motion, used in clocks to measure time.

stem: The distance between two cities is measured in __________, while the time for the journey is measured in __________.
solution: Long distances are measured in kilometres and journey times in hours.

stem: A body at rest on a distance–time graph shows __________.
options: no change in distance with time
solution: At rest, distance stays constant with time — a horizontal line.

stem: A vehicle moving at 72 km/h has a speed in m/s of __________.
The clock based on the swinging pendulum was developed after studying the regular swing observed by __________.
solution: Galileo studied the regular period of a swinging pendulum, which later led to pendulum clocks.

stem: An object taking a shorter time to cover a given distance has a __________ speed.
solution: For the same distance, less time taken means a higher speed.

stem: The unit of speed 'm/s' is derived from the units of __________.
solution: Speed is distance/time, so its unit combines metre (distance) and second (time).

stem: Which of the following describes uniform speed?
options: A car moving at a steady 40 km/h on a straight road
A car speeding up and slowing down
A stone falling faster and faster
solution: Uniform speed means the object covers equal distances in equal times, e.g., a steady 40 km/h.

stem: The amplitude of a pendulum is the __________.
options: maximum displacement of the bob from its central rest position
solution: Amplitude is the maximum distance the bob moves from its mean (central) position.

stem: The larger the distance covered in a fixed time, the __________ the average speed.
solution: Covering more distance in the same time means a greater average speed.

stem: Which of the following is a device from the past used to measure time by dripping water?
solution: A water clock measured time by the steady dripping or flow of water.

stem: A sand clock (hourglass) measures time using the __________.
options: steady flow of sand from one chamber to another
solution: An hourglass measures a fixed time interval by the steady flow of sand between its two bulbs.

stem: If an object's distance–time graph is a curve that gets steeper, the object is __________.
solution: A curve getting steeper means distance is covered faster with time — the object is speeding up.

stem: The average speed of a cyclist who rides 12 km in 30 minutes is __________.
solution: 30 minutes = 0.5 h; speed = 12 km ÷ 0.5 h = 24 km/h.

stem: Why were standard units of time and distance introduced?
options: To allow consistent and comparable measurements everywhere
solution: Standard units ensure that measurements of time and distance are consistent and comparable worldwide.

stem: A larger unit of time than the second includes the __________.
solution: Minute, hour and day are larger units of time than the second.

stem: A body covering 5 metres every second is moving at a speed of __________.
solution: Covering 5 m each second means a speed of 5 metres per second (5 m/s).

stem: The frequency of a pendulum is the number of __________ it makes per second.
solution: Frequency is the number of oscillations completed per second, the inverse of the time period.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Motion and Time' is that:
options: motion is described using speed (distance per unit time), and time is measured using periodic events such as the swing of a pendulum
solution: The chapter links motion to speed (distance/time) and shows how periodic motion, like a pendulum, is used to measure time, with distance–time graphs describing motion.

stem: The change in the position of an object with time is called:
solution: Motion is the change in the position of an object with respect to time; an object is said to be in motion if its position changes with time.

stem: The distance travelled by an object in a unit of time is called its:
solution: Speed is the distance travelled by an object per unit of time; it tells us how fast or slow an object is moving.

stem: The SI unit of speed is:
solution: The SI unit of speed is metre per second (m/s); speed is also commonly expressed in kilometres per hour (km/h).

stem: Speed is calculated as:
solution: Speed = distance ÷ time. So an object covering more distance in less time has a higher speed.

stem: An object that covers equal distances in equal intervals of time is said to be in:
solution: An object in uniform motion covers equal distances in equal intervals of time; its speed remains constant.

stem: An object that covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time is in:
solution: An object in non-uniform motion covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time; its speed keeps changing (e.g. a car in traffic).

stem: The motion of the hands of a clock is an example of:
solution: The hands of a clock move in a circle, so this is an example of circular motion; the blades of a fan also show circular motion.

stem: The to-and-fro (back-and-forth) motion of a pendulum is called:
solution: The to-and-fro motion of a simple pendulum about its mean position is called oscillatory or periodic motion; it repeats after a fixed time.

stem: The time taken by a pendulum to complete one full oscillation is called its:
solution: The time period of a pendulum is the time taken to complete one full oscillation (one to-and-fro swing); it is used as the basis of pendulum clocks.

stem: The device that measures time based on the regular oscillations of a pendulum is a:
solution: A pendulum clock uses the regular (constant) time period of a pendulum's oscillations to measure time accurately.

stem: The device fitted in vehicles that shows the speed at which the vehicle is moving is the:
solution: A speedometer is the device in a vehicle that shows the speed at which it is moving (usually in km/h).

stem: The device in a vehicle that measures the total distance travelled is the:
solution: An odometer measures and displays the total distance travelled by a vehicle.

stem: A distance-time graph for an object in uniform motion is a:
solution: For an object moving with uniform (constant) speed, the distance-time graph is a straight line, showing that distance increases at a steady rate with time.

stem: A distance-time graph for a stationary (at rest) object is:
options: A straight horizontal line (parallel to the time axis)
solution: For an object at rest, the distance does not change with time, so the distance-time graph is a straight horizontal line parallel to the time axis.

stem: The SI unit of time is the:
solution: The SI unit of time is the second (s); other units like minutes, hours and days are also used to measure time.

stem: Ancient people measured time using devices like the sundial and:
solution: Before modern clocks, people measured time using sundials (shadow of the Sun), water clocks and sand clocks (hourglasses).

stem: If a car travels 100 kilometres in 2 hours, its average speed is:
solution: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 100 km ÷ 2 h = 50 km/h.

stem: The larger the time period of a pendulum, the ______ its oscillation.
solution: A larger time period means the pendulum takes more time to complete one oscillation, so its swing is slower; the time period depends mainly on the length of the pendulum.

stem: The motion of the Earth around the Sun is an example of:
solution: The Earth's motion around the Sun (revolution) is a periodic motion, as it repeats after a fixed period (one year).

stem: Which statement about motion and time is correct? (i) Speed = distance/time (ii) SI unit of speed is m/s (iii) A pendulum shows periodic motion
solution: All three are correct: speed = distance/time, the SI unit of speed is metre per second, and a pendulum exhibits periodic (oscillatory) motion.

stem: The 'amplitude' of an oscillating pendulum is:
options: The maximum displacement from its mean (rest) position
solution: The amplitude of a pendulum is the maximum distance it moves from its mean (central rest) position on either side during oscillation.

stem: An object moving along a straight line is said to have:
solution: Rectilinear motion is motion along a straight line, such as a car moving on a straight road or a ball rolling straight.

stem: Which of the following correctly matches a device with its function? (i) Speedometer – speed (ii) Odometer – distance (iii) Pendulum clock – time
solution: All three are correct: a speedometer measures speed, an odometer measures distance, and a pendulum clock measures time.

stem: The overall importance of measuring motion and time is that it helps us:
options: Plan travel, run schedules, and understand and describe how things move
solution: Measuring motion and time is essential in daily life — for planning travel, running transport and schedules, sports, science and technology — helping us understand and describe how objects move.

stem: A simple pendulum's time period depends mainly on its:
solution: The time period of a simple pendulum depends mainly on the length of the pendulum (a longer pendulum has a longer time period); it does not depend on the mass of the bob.
